sample_unit: dermatologic images (two large-scale datasets; count not reported)

links.outcome: Gender bias and diagnostic performance after applying bias mitigation versus existing mitigation algorithms
links.effect: LesionAttn significantly mitigated gender bias while maintaining high diagnostic performance, outperforming existing bias-mitigation algorithms on two datasets (numbers not reported in abstract).
links.quote: Validated on two large-scale dermatologic datasets for binary malignancy classification, LesionAttn significantly mitigated gender bias while maintaining high diagnostic performance, outperforming existing bias-mitigation algorithms.

unlisted_practices: Attention-guided training directing model focus to lesions to reduce gender bias
Pareto Frontier dual-objective model selection balancing fairness and performance

screen.reason: The study develops and benchmarks a new algorithmic attention-guidance method (LesionAttn) to reduce gender bias on retrospective image datasets; it addresses fairness/bias but tests a new model architecture/training technique rather than an organizational deployment practice or operational safeguard.
